title: Circle reports $770 million Q4 revenue as USDC circulation reaches $75 billion, targets 40% CAGR for stablecoin description: Reserve income drove most of the quarterly gain, while Circle ended 2025 with $75.3 billion in USDC and set a 40% growth target.
Circle reports $770 million Q4 revenue as USDC circulation reaches $75 billion, targets 40% CAGR for stablecoin
<Circle reports $770 million Q4 revenue as USDC circulation reaches $75 billion, targets 40% CAGR for stablecoin>
* Circle reported Q4 revenue and reserve income of $770 million, a 77% increase from the prior year, as USDC in circulation rose to $75.3 billion.
* The company also issued multi-year guidance targeting a 40% compound annual growth rate for USDC in circulation.
Circle Internet Group Circle Internet Group, Inc.
(CRCL) posted $770 million in total revenue and reserve income for the fourth quarter of 2025, a 77% increase from the same period a year earlier, according to its Wednesday earnings report.
The New York-based stablecoin issuer ended the year with $75.3 billion in USDC circulation, up 72% from the end of 2024.
The revenue growth was driven primarily by reserve income, which reached $733 million in the quarter. Average USDC in circulation doubled year-over-year to $76.2 billion, though the reserve return rate declined 68 basis points to 3.8%, per the report.
Notably, the USDC issuer reported net income from continuing operations of $133 million for Q4, compared with $4 million in the prior-year period. Adjusted EBITDA for the quarter hit $167 million, a 412% increase from Q4 2024.
The loss was significantly impacted by $424 million in stock-based compensation tied to vesting conditions triggered by its initial public offering.
Meanwhile, the company also issued multi-year guidance targeting a 40% compound annual growth rate for USDC in circulation.
If sustained, that growth rate could significantly expand USDC’s share of the stablecoin market, currently led by Tether with roughly $183 billion in circulation, according to The Block’s data dashboard.

Beyond core financials and USDC expansion, Circle reported growth across its digital asset offerings. EURC in circulation reached €310 million at year-end, a 284% increase from the prior year and 44% higher than the third quarter.

results.title: Circle faces 'medium-term' risks from slow USDC growth, rising distribution costs: Mizuho
excerpts:
* Mizuho Securities equities researchers say Circle’s stock faces medium-term risks from slower-than-expected USDC growth, rising distribution costs, and a potential Fed rate cut.
The amount of USDC in circulation grew by 90% year-over-year to $61.3 billion, while the company’s total revenue and reserve income increased by 53% to $658 million.
And yet, Circle’s stock has started to "fade," according to Mizuho Securities equities researchers. The analysts see three possible reasons for the stock’s surprising underperformance.
Namely, there is a growing divide between USDC's “dreams” and “reality” of distribution. While the stablecoin saw 6% QTD growth amid rising interest in crypto, this falls short of the company’s outlook of achieving a long-term compound annual growth rate of 40%.
Already, several major institutions have signaled interest in launching or introducing stablecoins, and Circle’s biggest rival, Tether, is working on a reentry plan into U.S. markets.
Finally, the analysts say, while "cooling CPI is good news for the economy but bad news for CRCL." On Tuesday, the Labor Department reported that U.S.
consumer prices rose 2.7% year over year in July, slightly below estimates, which raised some expectations that the Federal Reserve could cut interest rates.
"But this isn't good news for CRCL, which benefits from higher rates," Mizuho wrote Wednesday in a note to clients, explaining its base case for CRCL’s performance.
"Given CRCL's dependence on a single macro factor (interest rates) and the potential for slower-than-expected USDC in circulation growth, we assign a market multiple to our below-consensus 2027E EBITDA to arrive at our PT of $84."
This is based on the fact that Circle's peer group, including Visa, Coinbase, and Robinhood, is currently trading around 23x EBITDA. A bear case accounts for slower-than-anticipated USDC growth of just 15% CAGR through 2027 to a $72 billion market cap, as well as lower interest rates to arrive at a price point of $40.
Of note, Bernstein analysts maintained a $230 price target on the stock.
Circle went public in June in a blockbuster IPO that saw shares rocket over 200% to over $90 per share on its first trading day. Shares are now trading hands at around $153.16 with a $41.1 billion market cap, according to The Block’s data.

results.title: Circle: Understanding the Company Behind USDC
excerpts:
As of September 18, 2026, approximately $72.9 billion of USDC was in circulation. Circle says USDC is backed by highly liquid cash and cash-equivalent assets, with reserves equal to or greater than the amount of USDC in circulation. Circle also publishes monthly reserve attestations from a Big Four accounting firm.
Circle's business model is unusual because its largest source of revenue comes from the assets backing USDC rather than from charging users a conventional transaction fee for holding the stablecoin.
The basic mechanism is straightforward. When USDC is issued, Circle holds reserve assets against the tokens in circulation.
Reserve income is the financial engine behind Circle's current business. Circle invests the reserves backing USDC in highly liquid assets, including cash and short-duration U.S. government securities and related instruments. As USDC circulation increases, the amount of reserves generating income also increases.
Interest rates therefore matter significantly to Circle. When short-term interest rates are high, the yield generated by USDC reserves can increase, boosting reserve income. Conversely, falling interest rates can put pressure on revenue even if the amount of USDC in circulation continues to grow.
This creates an important relationship for CRCL investors:
USDC circulation × reserve yield = a major component of Circle's revenue potential.
However, Circle does not keep all of the economics generated by USDC reserves. One of the most important examples is its relationship with Coinbase.
Several factors can influence CRCL because Circle sits at the intersection of the crypto market, financial markets, and the stablecoin industry.
USDC circulation is one of the most important factors. A larger USDC supply generally means a larger pool of reserves generating income.
Circle reported that USDC circulation reached roughly $73 billion in the second quarter of 2026, while its broader strategy continues to target stablecoin adoption across exchanges, financial institutions, payments companies, and other applications.
Interest rates are another major factor.
Because Circle earns income from USDC reserves, changes in short-term interest rates can affect the amount of revenue generated from a given level of USDC circulation. A growing USDC supply can partially offset lower yields, but the two variables should be considered separately.
Distribution costs are equally important.
Circle pays Coinbase and other ecosystem participants to distribute and promote USDC. As a result, investors need to look not only at reserve income but also at how much of that income Circle retains after distribution expenses.
Changes in interest-rate expectations, regulatory developments, USDC circulation, and announcements involving major distribution partners have all become relevant to the stock's performance.
As of September 23, 2026, CRCL was trading at approximately $94.82, compared with a 52-week range of $49.90 to $159.47.
